title: Crypto glossary
description: Plain-English definitions of the crypto and memecoin trading terms used across this guide.
summary: 48 terms in plain English, each linked to where it matters.

items.def: Scammers send tiny transfers from look-alike addresses, hoping you'll copy the wrong one from your history.
Free tokens a project sends to early users. Claim only through the project's official links.
To buy fast, without research. It usually ends badly.
Annual percentage yield, including compounding. In crypto it's usually variable.
All-time high: the highest price a coin has ever reached.
A pricing formula that raises the price as more people buy. Launchpads like pump.fun use one before a coin 'graduates' to a normal market.
When the creator buys a big share of a new coin, often across many wallets, in the very first block, so they can dump on later buyers.
A separate wallet holding only a small amount, used for risky sites and trades.
Centralized exchange, such as Coinbase or Binance. A company holds your coins for you.
A wallet whose keys stay offline, usually a hardware device. Best for savings.
The person or team who created a token. 'Dev sold' means the creator dumped their coins.
Decentralized exchange. You swap directly from your own wallet through smart contracts.
A malicious site or script that tricks you into signing a transaction that empties your wallet.
Do your own research.
Your average profit or loss per trade over many trades: (win rate x average win) minus (loss rate x average loss), after costs.
Fully diluted valuation: the price multiplied by every token that will ever exist, not just the ones trading today.
The fee you pay the blockchain to process your transaction.
When a launchpad coin fills its bonding curve and moves to a regular DEX pool.
A small device that stores your keys offline and signs transactions on its own screen. Buy only from the maker.
A token you can buy but cannot sell.
A wallet app on an internet-connected phone or computer. Convenient, but more exposed.
Key opinion leader: an influencer whose posts move prices. Some are paid to promote.
A token, like stETH or JitoSOL, that represents staked coins and keeps earning while you hold it.
How much money sits in a trading pool. Low liquidity means big price moves and hard exits.
A pool of two tokens that traders swap against. 'LP burned' means the creator can't pull the pool's money out.
Price x circulating supply. It's a better guide than price alone to how 'big' a coin already is.
A token driven by jokes, culture and attention rather than a product. Extremely volatile.
When bots see your trade coming and trade just before and after it, profiting from your slippage.
The power to create new tokens. If it isn't revoked, the creator can print supply and dump it.
A wallet whose key is split into pieces held in different places, so there is no single seed phrase.
A wallet that needs several keys (for example 2 of 3) to approve a transaction.
Not financial advice.
A leveraged contract that tracks a coin's price with no expiry date. Leverage can wipe you out fast.
An extra tip paid to get your transaction processed faster. It adds up quickly in memecoin trading.
The amount you're willing to lose on one trade. A 3R win is three times that amount.
Cancel a token approval, for example with revoke.cash.
When a creator pulls the liquidity or dumps their supply, leaving holders with worthless tokens.
The 12 or 24 backup words that control your wallet. Anyone who has them owns your crypto. Never share them.
Holding your own keys rather than leaving coins on an exchange.
The difference between the price you expected and the price you got. It's large on small coins.
A token designed to stay at $1, like USDC or USDT.
Locking coins to help run a proof-of-stake network in return for rewards.
A price at which you sell to cap your loss.
Token generation event: when a token launches and starts trading.
Exiting a trade because it hasn't worked within a set time, whatever the price.
Permission you give a smart contract to move your tokens. Unlimited approvals are a major drainer risk, so revoke old ones.
Total value locked: how much money is deposited in a protocol.
A wallet holding a very large amount of a coin.
